description.narrative: Benin Terminal (BT or the Company), the concessionaire of the container terminal of the port of Cotonou (the Port), has embarked on a EUR 165.5 million investment plan to upgrade its terminal and purchase new equipment (the Project). This Project is embedded in the wider expansion program of the Port under the coordination of Port Autonome de Cotonou (PAC), the state-owned entity in charge of the management and development of the Port. The initial concession between BT, PAC and the State of Benin was signed in 2009. In July 2022, as part of the PAC expansion program, the parties signed a new concession of 27 years.

The main project-level outcomes are expected from the positive effects on stakeholders through the modernization of the Benin Terminal, which will lead to improved container handling efficiency and service quality, enabling greater container volumes. The project is also expected to have economy-wide effects as the port handles 90% of Benin's international trade and is central to its economy. The expansion is expected to contribute to increased growth and indirect jobs in Benin and hinterland markets. Beyond the Project, this investment is expected to strengthen Benin Terminal competitiveness and regional trade integration as the port serves as the closest access corridor for landlocked Niger and as an alternate access point for Malian and Burkinabe goods imports/exports, while providing alternate access to the northern states of Nigeria.
